extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners and applicants (patent attorneys, agents, and inventors) looking up examiner behavior and grant likelihood
extracted.subtask_description: Using Patent Bots' examiner statistics to estimate an examiner's grant likelihood and timing, compare examiners, and explore USPTO-level grant rate distributions and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year grant rate (3YGR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 3-year grant rate (3YGR) is the percentage of applications granted by 3 years after the first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Our grant rate is based on a timeline of dispositions of applications. To compare examiners, we use the 3-year grant rate (3YGR). This metric is intended to show how likely you are to get a patent and also when you are likely to get it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant rate timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: A timeline of dispositions where the timeline is relative to the date of the first office action; shows grant rate at different times after the first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example timeline here is for the entire USPTO, and we also have timelines for each examiner. The three-year grant rate is the percentage of applications granted at three years after the first office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset inclusion criteria (time window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current dataset includes all utility patent applications filed in 2010 or later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives plenty of data for computing 3-year grant rates but also allows focus on more recent data in case an examiner's behavior changes over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted histogram of examiner grant rates
rubrics_metrics.description: A weighted histogram (by number of cases) of the 3-year grant rates of the examiners in USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides distributional context (the page reports an average of 77% and a standard deviation of 17%). Weighting by number of cases emphasizes examiners with more data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation note on time-varying percentages and shrinking sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: For large enough data sets, the percentage of grants and abandonments will always be increasing over time; for some examiners the number of grants and abandonments can decrease over time because the size of the data set is shrinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users should interpret declines in counts or percentages with caution, recognizing that they may be artifacts of smaller sample sizes as the timeline moves forward rather than true changes in examiner behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative use of metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 3YGR and timelines to compare examiners and estimate how likely and how quickly you might obtain a patent under a given examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site explicitly states the purpose: 'This shows you how likely you are to get a patent and also when you are likely to get it.' Comparisons across examiners should be based on the 3YGR and the timeline visualizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search, browse, and visualization tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Search by examiner name; browse the USPTO hierarchy of tech centers, groups, and art units; view scatter plots of examiners according to grant rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tools are provided to locate specific examiners, explore patterns by art unit or tech center, and visualize examiner-level grant-rate variation (e.g., scatter plot of grant rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and liability disclaimer
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not provide any guarantees as to the accuracy of the statistics presented above and under no circumstances will we be liable for any outcome resulting from your reliance on the above statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the statistics as informational estimates rather than definitive predictions; users bear responsibility for reliance and should corroborate with other sources when making high-stakes decisions.
